newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani private airline seeks partner.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani private airline seeks partner.

text.p: A private Pakistani airline, Shaheen Airlines International (SAI ), is seeking a partner for a joint venture to resume suspended domestic services, Air Force chief Air Chief Marshal Abbass Khattak said on Wednesday.

SAI, owned by the air force business and welfare group Shaheen Foundation, suspended domestic services when two Boeing 737s leased from the Thai Airways were withdrawn in May 1996 after talks about buying them broke down.
But it continued flying between the northwestern town of Peshawar and Dubai with a leased Airbus.
"We are trying to revive our domestic service through a joint venture," Khattak said. "We are hopeful we get a partner soon."
Shaheen Foundation, in joint venture with Canada's Edmonton-based CAE Aviation Ltd, already has an engineering facility in Islamabad for routine aircraft maintenance.
SAI suffered cumulative losses of 250 to 350 million rupees ($7.2-10 million) from the start of its operations in 1993 to the end of fiscal 1995/96 (July-June), airline sources said.
